risk_reasons: Changes three customer-facing and admin-facing email send paths in worker/jobs/, which invariant #1 places on the Railway worker.
Changes src/lib/approval/create-link.ts, shared approval-link code governed by invariant #5 and the approval-security skill.
A wrong 409 classification either drops a real email or re-sends a delivered one; both are silent to the owner.
goal: A crash between the Resend send and the local sent-marker in OnboardingDripWorker and EngagementAlertWorker no longer delivers a second copy of the same email, and the approval link carried by the first copy stays usable.
non_goals: Reordering any send site to mark-before-send. The owner chose the provider idempotency key for all three sites.
Changing the partner satisfaction alert branch (EngagementAlertWorker.ts:400). It already marks the Outbox job completed before sending, so a key adds nothing there.
Adding an outbox reference column to notification_deliveries. That is a migration and rides its own PR.
Making sendInternalEmail require an idempotency key, or adding a CI audit that forces one on new call sites.
Changing the two approval-link call sites outside this ticket (worker/jobs/notification/dispatch.ts, worker/jobs/pending-post-notice/dispatch.ts). Their revoke behaviour stays exactly as it is.
Changing the Drip staleness cap, the onboarding_drip_log claim protocol, or the EngagementMonitorPoller cooldown guards.
user_visible_behavior: A business owner whose onboarding drip job crashes after Resend accepted the email receives exactly one copy, not two.
A business owner whose owner nudge job crashes after Resend accepted the email receives exactly one copy, not two.
The admin inbox receives exactly one partner engagement, escalation, or low-engagement alert per occurrence, not two.
An approval link delivered in a Day 7 drip or an owner nudge keeps working after the job retries, instead of being revoked by the retry that builds a replacement link.
Operators can tell a suppressed duplicate from a genuine send: the notification_deliveries row for a suppressed duplicate carries external_message_id prefixed 'idempotent-replay:'.
invariants: #5 Approval tokens never stored raw. createApprovalLink keeps generating randomUUID tokens and storing only SHA-256 hashes; revokeMode 'never' changes only whether prior links are revoked.
#2 The Outbox job stays the unit of work. No send site starts writing Postgres and separately enqueueing BullMQ.
#12 Entry points orchestrate; modules own failure behavior. The Resend 409 classification lives in sendInternalEmail, not in either worker.
#10 Node.js native crypto only. No new hashing, no crypto-js.
#11 The subscription guard ordering in both workers is untouched.
Approval links keep their 48-hour TTL, so revokeMode 'never' leaves at most one extra live link per response and it expires on its own.
Regenerate still revokes every outstanding link for a response. revokeMode 'never' does not weaken that path.
edge_cases: Resend returns 'invalid_idempotent_request' (409): the same key was submitted with a different body, which proves Resend already accepted the first email. Treat as a successful send. This is the normal retry path for the Day 7 drip and the owner nudge, whose bodies change because createApprovalLink mints a fresh token per call.
Resend returns 'concurrent_idempotent_requests' (409): the first request is still in flight, which is NOT proof of acceptance. Throw, so BullMQ retries later.
Resend returns 'invalid_idempotency_key': the key we built is malformed. Throw. This is a programming error, not a delivery outcome.

A Resend idempotency key expires after 24 hours. A retry or a Watchdog re-dispatch beyond that window sends a second email. Accepted: every retry path here completes in minutes, and no durable guarantee is claimed.
Mock mode (MOCK_EXTERNAL_APIS=true) returns early in sendInternalEmail before any Resend call, so no key is sent and no 409 can occur. Behaviour is unchanged.

The onboarding drip stale-claim takeover (OnboardingDripWorker.ts:227-236) lets a SECOND outbox row take over a claim left with sent_at IS NULL. Two rows carry two outbox ids, so the drip key is scoped to (business_id, drip_type) instead, matching onboarding_drip_log UNIQUE(business_id, drip_type).
The owner nudge and the partner alerts recur on a cooldown and have no natural domain identity, so their keys are scoped to the outbox row id, which is the identity of one send occurrence.
An idempotent replay yields no Resend message id. recordNotificationDelivery still requires a string, so the replay records 'idempotent-replay:<key>'.

A Day 7 drip or owner nudge whose pending response already has an approval_request or pending_post_notice delivery was never revoked under orphaned_only. revokeMode 'never' is a superset of that behaviour, so those cases are unaffected.
An owner nudge with zero pending reviews returns before any send, so it never builds a key.

rollback_plan: Revert the single squash-merged commit. No migration, no schema change, no feature flag, no env var. Reverting restores the pre-change send order and the orphaned_only revoke behaviour at both approval-link call sites; the only lasting trace is the 'idempotent-replay:' prefix on any notification_deliveries rows written while the change was live, which is inert data.
observability: Each worker logs a distinct line on an idempotent replay, naming the worker, the business id and the key, so a suppressed duplicate is greppable in the Railway worker logs.

notification_deliveries.external_message_id prefixed 'idempotent-replay:' is the durable record: SELECT count(*) FROM notification_deliveries WHERE external_message_id LIKE 'idempotent-replay:%' counts suppressed duplicates after release.
A rise in terminal failures on the onboarding_drip or engagement_alert topics after release would indicate the 409 classification is wrong; the Job-failure sink raises those to Sentry already.
